newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian officials deny vote count under threat.
newsitem.headline: Albanian officials deny vote count under threat.

text.p: European envoy Franz Vranitzky said on Thursday that the count in Albania's general election was under threat from a lack of cooperation by electoral workers but a top Albanian official denied the allegation.

In a statement issued in Vienna by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, the former Austrian chancellor urged electoral officials to complete the tasks in bringing in the vote from Sunday's first round.
"Several members of the Central Election Commission (CEC), apparently under political pressure, have stopped participating in the authorising process," the statement said.

"If the absent members do not return immediately, they should be replaced in order to proceed with the election the Albanian people so clearly desire. Additionally, the CEC is still awaiting the results from 20 zones, also seemingly due to political interference."
But the head of the electoral commission denied officials were absent or under pressure from anyone. He said everything was being done to complete the count and announce the results.
"This commission will not be influenced by pressure from any party or anyone else," Kristaq Kume told Albanian state television.

"I reject the allegation that members of the election commission have left. Quite the opposite...The commission is working on the results and is expecting documents from certain districts, which is delaying the announcement of the results."
Incomplete returns from Sunday's first round have given the Socialists under economist Fatos Nano a big lead.

President Sali Berisha has admitted the defeat of his Democratic Party and said he will step down when a leftist government comes to power. Run-off elections will be held on Sunday in districts where no candidate got the required 50 percent of the vote.

Vranitzky helped broker an agreement in March between Albania's bickering political parties to form a multi-party interim government and proceed with the early election. Both Berisha and Socialist leaders have thanked him for the role he played in organising the election.
